paragraphs: Ship Engineers (53-5031) handle onboard engineering operation and maintenance; marine engineers and naval architects, deck officers, sailors and oilers, and motorboat mechanics focus respectively on design, navigation, basic onboard work, and shore repairs.
Marine engineers and naval architects design, develop, and evaluate hull, propulsion, and ship system designs.
Suitable for people willing to handle calculations, drawings, model tests, and design reviews; engineering watch experience may provide operating feedback.
Design positions deliver engineering designs; ship engineers deliver onboard operating, repair, and handoff records.
Marine Engineers and Naval Architects (17-2121)
Captains, mates, and pilots direct navigation, routes, maneuvering, and bridge watches.
Suitable for people interested in navigation decisions, ship maneuvering, and deck teams; check competency conditions for corresponding deck duties.
Bridge and engine room work closely together, but navigation command and main engine maintenance have different authorizations and certificates.
Captains and Mates (53-5021)
Sailors and marine oilers perform basic deck or engineering maintenance, watch support, and assistance with equipment operation.
Suitable for people building operating observation and handoff experience through trained basic onboard positions.
Support-level positions differ in duties and competency scope from management- or operational-level engineering duties.
Sailors and Marine Oilers (53-5011)
Motorboat mechanics inspect, repair, and adjust marine engines and related machinery, often in boat repair or service settings.
Suitable for people who enjoy dismantling, repairing, shore-based workstations, and diagnosing specific engine faults.
Repair tasks overlap with onboard watches, but shore mechanics do not automatically receive seagoing engineering competency.
Motorboat Mechanics (49-3051)
Monitor main engines, generators, and pumps during onboard shifts, handle alarms, and hand over information to chief engineers and the bridge.
Suitable for people who accept offshore living, continuous monitoring, and strict reporting chains; duties must remain within certificate scope.
An internal setting emphasizing equipment operation during voyages; not all engineer officers may independently direct the engine room.
Internal setting: sea watchkeeping
Communicate fault evidence, spare-part needs, and retest results between vessels and shore repair, material, and technical personnel.
Suitable for people who understand actual engine-room conditions and communicate with shore teams through work orders.
An internal setting; shore coordination does not equal ship design or automatically confer purchasing budget approval.
Internal setting: shore technical coordination

First determine whether the target is sea engineering watchkeeping or shore design and repair, then compare equipment, qualifications, trading areas, and living conditions. Engineering experience may transfer, but target positions require actual supporting evidence.
